llm._hedge_note: If DeepSeek hasn't answered after hedge_after_ms, the same request is sent again and the first answer wins (cuts rare 5-13 s waits; costs ~a few % more calls). 0 = off.

data._note: Promo codes are off by default: many are given to specific customers. Discounts are always applied by the POS, never by the assistant.

context._note: The whole live menu, FAQ and delivery areas go into the prompt with every message (decided 2026-11-09, replaces vector search for the menu).

chunking._note: Types in whole_document_types are always one chunk. Longer text (FAQ answers) is split on paragraphs/sentences into pieces of at most max_chars, each starting with its question, with overlap_chars carried over from the previous piece.

assistant._hours_note: null = always on. Example: {"open": "12:00", "close": "02:00"} (closing after midnight is fine). Outside hours the assistant stays quiet; staff see the messages.
assistant._enabled_note: Starts OFF so a newly linked number never auto-replies by surprise. Switch it on with the 🤖 Auto-reply button in the Cashier WhatsApp screen (the choice is remembered).

embedding.status: not used for now: the menu fits in the prompt. Kept as the option if FAQs grow very large

stt._note: Voice notes are transcribed by Groq's hosted Whisper large-v3 (needs GROQ_API_KEY in .env; about $0.11 per hour of audio, 10 s minimum per note). Whisper's language auto-detect is unreliable for Urdu, so the language is fixed.
stt._cleanup_note: After transcription, DeepSeek rewrites the whole transcript into what the customer most likely said (Roman Urdu), using the menu (rag/prompts/voice-cleanup.md). Tested on real notes: recovers 'order', 'menu', 'Double Patty', 'discount' from garbled text. Falls back to the raw transcript if it fails.
